§5.5 Embedded Pages

📄 Page rule — applied from the page alone

layout-embedded-pages · rule layout legal

✅ Normative

A page reproduced inside another page MUST be rendered as the wrapper's furniture followed by the embedded page in its own reading order. Both page numbers MUST be kept, each with its own region, and titles inside an embedded form screenshot MUST NOT be promoted into the wrapper's outline.

A page reproduced inside another page: a statute page shrunk into the middle of an exhibit sheet, a slide placed on a letter-size page. Each carries its own header and page number, so the sheet has two of everything.

      Case 1:23-cv-06750   Document 1-4   Filed 08/02/23   Page 4 of 4     ← wrapper header
                              EXHIBIT D
                          ┌────────────────────┐
                          │   H. R. 2617—507   │  ← embedded header
                          │   (1) The term …   │
                          └────────────────────┘
                              Page 3 of 3                                  ← wrapper footer

Requirements

  • The wrapper's label and filing stamp MUST be kept: they identify the particular copy.
  • The embedded content MUST appear between the wrapper header and the wrapper footer, in the embedded page's own reading order.
  • The wrapper's page number and the embedded page's number MUST both be kept, each where its own band prints it.
  • A title printed inside an embedded form screenshot MUST NOT become a heading of the wrapping document.

✅ Sample — a statute page as an exhibit

A blue e-filing header in four parts, a red EXHIBIT D label, then a reduced statute page with its own running head H. R. 2617—507, and a red Page 3 of 3 at the foot. Expected boxes: four Page-header elements for the e-filing line, Text for EXHIBIT D, a Page-header for the embedded running head, one Text per statute paragraph, and a Page-footer for Page 3 of 3. The colours are decoration and are not carried.
